one-check-per-line.why: all 4 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 4

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

words-only.why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against the words of its expect line. Check 1 tests export type, zero fill, the default space and a '*' fill. Each case is "padded on the left with fill… to exactly width characters", which the words require. Check 2 tests only the equal-length and longer cases. Check 3 requires a heading naming each exported function, followed by some text describing it. That fits a reasonable reading of "a section for every function". Its list of the four names comes from the repository facts and adds no test the words don't force. Check 4 only requires passing tests and a successful exit. The test-coverage check and the multi-character fill note are correctly placed under "Advisory". No PASS or FAIL condition contains a mutation test, a branch rule, a file-scope rule or an exact-wording requirement.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs. `npm test` matches the package.json script, and the `node --input-type=module -e` commands in Checks 1 and 2 use valid shell quoting and valid JS. Check 3 breaks. Its JS sits inside a double-quoted bash string that contains `new RegExp('\\b' + f + '\\b')`. Inside double quotes, bash turns `\\` into `\`, so node receives `'\b'`. In a JS string, `'\b'` is a backspace character, not a regex word boundary. No README heading contains a backspace, so the test never matches. The command would print every export as `missing:`, even for a correct README. Run as written, this check gives a wrong result. The command does not work as intended in this repository, so the criterion fails for the whole output.

catches-traps.why: I checked all three must_catch items, and the briefs handle each one. (1) Builder step 3 asks for a padLeft section "AND add the missing section for slugify (heading `## slugify(s)`...)". (2) Verifier Check 3 prints the exports, says they "must include capitalize, slugify, truncate and padLeft", and FAILs "if any exported function is listed as missing (note: slugify had no README section before this change)". (3) Verifier Check 1 calls `p('ab',4)` with no fill argument and expects "  ab", which checks the default space padding. No part of either brief breaks the criterion.

avoids-must-not.why: Item 1: Check 3 lists every exported function and requires a README heading naming each one (word-boundary regex). A README with padLeft but no slugify section prints "missing: slugify" and fails; the brief also says "slugify had no README section before this change". Item 2: Checks 1–2 only test results that follow from lines 1–2 ("00042", "  ab", "**x", unchanged inputs). Nothing checks the parameter count or that fill is one character; multi-character fill is advisory ("do not fail on it"). Check 3 accepts any heading level, needing only that the heading names the function and has some text under it. That is the plain Markdown idea of a section, not a forced layout. The exact `## name(args)` format appears only in the builder brief. Check 4 only requires npm test to pass. Nothing on the must_not list is present.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief's examples with the verifier brief's probes. Step 1 of the builder brief gives "padLeft('42', 5, '0') === '00042'; padLeft('ab', 4) === '  ab'". Check 1 of the verifier brief runs p('42',5,'0') and p('ab',4) and expects "00042" and "  ab". Those are the same inputs with the same expected outputs. Step 2 also tells the builder to write tests for exactly those cases. The builder's 'abcdef', 3 example is also close to Check 2's p('abcdef',3,'0'). So the builder brief contains part of the verifier's probe set, not just the bar. Telling the builder to run npm test and write its own tests is allowed. Sharing the checker's exact input/output pairs is not, so the criterion fails.
